paragrafos.a: The site has no accounts, no analytics tools, and sets no cookies for visitors. But, as with any website, each visit goes through a server: the hosting service (Vercel) logs the requests it receives — the network address (IP), the page requested, the date and time, and the browser identification — to deliver the pages and protect the site from abuse. We don't use these logs to find out who is who.
paragrafos.b: The legal basis is our legitimate interest in keeping the site running and secure (GDPR, Art. 6(1)(f)). These logs are kept for the retention period of the hosting plan.
paragrafos.c: When you open the menu through a table's QR code or NFC tag, the server records the table number and the time: it adds the scan to that table's counts, per night and per hour, and keeps the last 300 scans with their exact time, so we know whether the codes are used. It does not store the network address, cookies or any identifier of the phone; the browser type is read only to leave out bots, and is not stored. The counts have no time limit, being just numbers; the list of recent scans is deleted if a year goes by without any.

pedidos.titulo: When you give us an email

paragrafos.a: The newsletter invitation and the secret menu ask for an email address. When you ask to sign up, we send you an email with a link to confirm. To do so, the address goes to the email delivery service (Resend), which keeps a record of the sending — recipient, subject and delivery status — for the account's retention period. If you don't confirm, the address is not added to any list.
paragrafos.b: To prevent abuse of these forms, the server counts requests in Upstash: per network address, for one hour, and per email, for 24 hours. The email is stored as a cryptographic digest (SHA-256): it isn't written down, but someone who already knows the address can match it — so we treat it as personal data, not as anonymous. If someone exceeds the limits, the server log keeps the network address and the partially hidden email, so the abuse can be understood.
paragrafos.c: The legal basis is your request (GDPR, Art. 6(1)(b)) and, for abuse control, our legitimate interest in protecting the service and other people's inboxes (Art. 6(1)(f)). Giving your email is optional; without it we can't send you the link.

paragrafos.a: If you ask for our news — in the site's invitation or in the secret menu — and confirm through the link, your email joins the mailing list (at Resend) and is used only to send you news from Café Preguiça, in Portuguese. The legal basis is your consent (GDPR, Art. 6(1)(a), and Portuguese Law 41/2004, Art. 13-A).
paragrafos.b: So that we can demonstrate that consent, we keep a record of each sign-up: when you asked and when you confirmed, where (invitation or secret menu), in which language, the sentence shown next to the request and the version of that text — and, if you unsubscribe, when and how. We don't store your network address or device for this. The record is kept in Upstash, identified by a digest of your email.
paragrafos.c: You can withdraw your consent at any time, free of charge: every newsletter has a link to unsubscribe, effective immediately, and you can also ask us through the contacts above. If you have already opened the secret menu on a device, unsubscribing does not close it there. Withdrawing consent does not make earlier emails unlawful.
paragrafos.d: Unsubscribing and erasure are different things. If you unsubscribe, you stop receiving emails and the address stays on the list marked as unsubscribed — that mark is what stops you receiving them again — until you ask us to erase it. The record of the sign-up and of the unsubscription is kept for three years after you unsubscribe, so we can answer a complaint about emails sent while you were subscribed, and is then deleted automatically. If you ask for erasure, we remove the address from the list and delete that record.

paragrafos.a: The secret menu is an extra for people who receive the café's news: you enter your email, and if it's on the list the menu opens; if not, you can sign up right there. To do this we ask Resend whether the address is subscribed, without storing it; to stop anyone guessing addresses, the server counts requests per network address for one hour. If you'd rather not leave your email, ask for the secret menu at the bar.
paragrafos.b: Once opened, your browser stores a key that opens it again — without your email inside it. By default it lasts until you close the tab; if you choose “remember on this device”, it lasts 90 days. The key doesn't depend on staying subscribed. The details are on the <cookies>cookies</cookies> page.

paragrafos.a: People who work at the café sign in to a reserved area with a code sent to them by email. We use each staff member's email to send them the code (through Resend) and keep, in Upstash: the pending code, as a digest, with the email, for 10 minutes; the session, for 8 hours; if the person asks us to remember the device, that device's token, for 30 days; and a log of each sign-in and sign-out — email, date and time, and the type of device and browser (e.g. “iPhone · Safari”) — for at most 30 days each. The network address is not kept in that log.
paragrafos.b: To limit attempts, the server counts code requests per email (as a digest) and per network address, over periods from 15 minutes to a day; failed attempts are kept in the server log with the network address and the partially hidden email. Changes published through the staff area are kept in the site's version history (on GitHub), with the partially hidden email of whoever made them.
paragrafos.c: The legal basis is the business's legitimate interest in protecting access to the reserved area and knowing who made each change (GDPR, Art. 6(1)(f)). None of this concerns people who only visit the site.

paragrafos.a: We use service providers that process data on our behalf: Vercel (site hosting), Resend (sending emails and the newsletter list), Upstash (counters, staff-area logs and the consent record) and GitHub (where the site's code and content live, including the history of changes made in the staff area). DevPlus, which builds and maintains the site, has access to these services to manage them. We don't sell data or share it for advertising.
paragrafos.b: None of these services runs in your browser: fonts and images come from this domain, there are no embedded maps or social media buttons, and the links to Google Maps and social networks are plain links that only open if you click them.

paragrafos.a: Resend stores contacts and sending records in the United States. Vercel, Upstash and GitHub are companies based in the United States and may process data there. In those cases, the transfer relies on the standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission, which are part of these providers' data processing agreements, and, where the provider is certified, on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. You can ask us for information about these safeguards through the contacts above.

conservacao.intro: There is no single legal retention period for this data: each item is kept for as long as its purpose requires.

itens.copias: Backups and the providers' internal logs follow each service's own periods: what we delete may take that long to disappear from them.

paragrafos.a: You can ask us for access to your data, rectification, erasure or restriction of processing, and object to processing based on our legitimate interest. For data you gave us based on your consent or your request, you can also ask for a copy in a commonly used format (portability). We reply within one month. We don't make automated decisions or create profiles.
paragrafos.b: If you believe your data has not been handled properly, you can lodge a complaint with the Portuguese data protection authority (<cnpd>CNPD</cnpd>).

ficha.noSitio: No: choices are asked where they're used

uso.texto: Visitors don't get cookies: there are no analytics, advertising or third-party cookies. The site keeps a few small notes in your browser, explained below — only the ones needed for what you asked for, or the ones you choose to keep. That's why there is no general banner: when a choice is yours, you're asked for it where it is used.

lingua.titulo: What about the language you chose?
lingua.texto: It lives in the address, not in a cookie: the English version is at /en. It stays while you browse the site. If you type the address again without /en, the site opens in Portuguese.

memoria.titulo: What stays in the browser's storage
memoria.intro: None of these notes is a cookie: they aren't sent with requests to the server (the menu key is only sent when the menu opens) and don't leave your device in any other way.

itens.convite: preguica:newsletter, in session storage: “inscrito” (signed up) or “fechado” (closed), so the newsletter invitation doesn't show up again during the same visit. The browser deletes it when you close the tab. It identifies no one.
itens.naoMostrar: preguica:newsletter:nao-mostrar, in local storage: only if you click “Don't show again on this device” in the invitation. It stores the date until which the invitation won't appear — six months — and is deleted afterwards.
itens.carta: preguica:carta-secreta, in session storage: the key that opens the secret menu after you've opened it once. Signed by us, without your email inside it, valid for 24 hours and deleted when you close the tab.
itens.cartaLembrada: preguica:carta-secreta, in local storage: the same key, only if you choose “remember on this device”. Valid for 90 days from your choice, without renewing, and the site deletes it afterwards; “Close the menu on this device” deletes it at once.
itens.painel: preguica:painel:seccoes-fechadas, in session storage and only in the staff area: which menu sections are collapsed in the editor.

equipa.texto: In the area reserved for people who work at the café — and only there: these cookies don't travel to other pages — there are up to three cookies. preguica_desafio holds the sign-in code in progress (10 minutes); preguica_sessao keeps the session open (8 hours); and preguica_aparelho, only if the person signing in ticks “Remember this device”, avoids asking for the code for 30 days. The first two are strictly necessary to sign in; the third is a choice, and “Forget this device” deletes it.

base.titulo: Why we don't ask permission for everything
base.texto: Portuguese law requires consent to store information on your device, except where it is strictly necessary for a service you asked for (Law 41/2004, Art. 5). The session notes and the two sign-in cookies fall into that case: they serve to open the menu you asked for, not to repeat an invitation you already answered, or to sign in to the staff area. The ones that last longer are only saved when you click the button or tick the box that says what is kept and for how long — and they are undone with those same buttons, or by clearing the site's data in your browser.

verificar.texto: You don't have to take our word for it: in your browser's developer tools, under the Application (or Storage) tab, you can see this domain's cookies, local storage and session storage. If you've never signed in to the staff area, you have no cookies from this site.

litigios.titulo: If you have a problem with us
litigios.texto: In a consumer dispute, you can turn to an alternative dispute resolution body. The one with jurisdiction over the area where the café is located is <entidade>{nome}</entidade>. Each centre has limits on what it handles — by value or by subject matter — and its website explains them. The list of bodies is on the <portal>Consumer Portal</portal> (in Portuguese).
litigios.adesao: The café has joined this centre.
litigios.reduzidoValor: In consumer disputes worth up to €5,000, if the consumer chooses to take the case to an authorised consumer arbitration centre, the café is bound by that arbitration or mediation (Portuguese Law 24/96, Art. 14).
litigios.pendente: The alternative dispute resolution body to be listed here is being confirmed with the business. Meanwhile, the official list of bodies is on the <portal>Consumer Portal</portal> (in Portuguese).

reclamacoes.texto: You can also file a complaint in the <livro>electronic Complaints Book</livro> (Livro de Reclamações Eletrónico).
